> DeskTouch is a touchscreen dashboard that sits on my desk. DeskTouch uses a Raspberry Pi and a 5‑inch touch display. I want DeskTouch to be an interface that shows a clock a calendar, a task list and a study timer. For the interface I will write HTML, CSS and JavaScript. A Python backend will be used only when it is needed. DeskTouch will run in full‑screen mode. Will have large buttons that are easy to touch. My first goal is to make a working clock, a task list and a timer. After those pieces are tested I will add features. I will also design a custom enclosure that's 3‑D printed. The enclosure will hold the screen give access to the power connector and have ventilation, for the Raspberry Pi. This project will combine interface design, programming, hardware assembly and CAD. I will document the development with photos, screenshots and a demonstration video.

### 2026-11-01: Please refer to the update on this project for the consolidated description of DeskTouch, its current direction and the next development steps. I am bringing the information there so that the project

**15h**

Please refer to the update on this project for the consolidated description of DeskTouch, its current direction and the next development steps. I am bringing the information there so that the project can be understood without having to reconstruct every decision from separate entries.

The project idea changed during the exploration. I first considered reusing a photo frame and its original controller board. I identified the board as AP_HI18CA_V1 and the main chip as HI1018A. However I did not establish a documented way to use that hardware for the dashboard I wanted to create.

I subsequently decided to move toward a Raspberry Pi with a touchscreen. The intended device is a desktop dashboard with a clock, calendar, task list and study timer. The latest update explains this revised concept and the planned work on the interface, enclosure and electrical connections.

Earlier entries should therefore be read as background to the project than as the final hardware specification. Component selection is still being evaluated, particularly because I want to reduce the cost while keeping the screen and computer compatible.The latest update also distinguishes planned work from completed observations. It does not claim that the enclosure has been manufactured, the electronics assembled or the dashboard tested. Those stages will require evidence as development continues. Please use that entry as the main reference, for the current project scope and remaining tasks.

### 2026-11-01: DeskTouch. Project Direction and Development Plan

**9h**

DeskTouch. Project Direction and Development Plan

DeskTouch is my project idea for a compact touchscreen dashboard that sits on a desk and provides everyday information. This update brings together the concept, the hardware direction and the work that remains before a functioning prototype can be demonstrated.

I initially explored reusing an existing photo frame. I identified its controller board as AP_HI18CA_V1. Its main chip as HI1018A. I did not confirm a suitable interface or development method for turning that hardware into an interactive dashboard so I decided to change direction.

The revised plan uses a Raspberry Pi and a compatible touchscreen. My initial reference configuration was a Raspberry Pi 4 with 2 GB of RAM and the official five-inch Touch Display 2. This is not yet a confirmed purchase: I am considering expensive options and need to compare the complete cost, including power supply, storage and enclosure materials.

The first software version is intended to show a clock, calendar, task list and study timer. I plan to use HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the touchscreen interface adding a Python backend where necessary.

The mechanical work will involve a custom enclosure with a screen, stable base, ventilation, internal mounting points and a removable cover. The electrical documentation will cover module connections, power requirements and assembly checks.

At this stage the work establishes the project direction and requirements. A completed CAD model, assembled circuit and working software prototype are not being claimed in this update. The next steps are to confirm components develop the enclosure and interface and document actual assembly and testing, with photographs and screenshots.
